route: /style-board/ (the style board: module process:timeline, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: The process:timeline steps have no step number or marker: each row is just a bold label beside text with a hairline under it, so it reads like a definitions table rather than an ordered sequence (the same at 390 px).
findings.reference: Every competitor step module numbers its steps: '01–03' in blue numerals on the three-step process, and a number over a title and text above a hairline on the six-step navy timeline (components.md).
findings.fix: In ProcessBlock.astro, render the step number (number(index), as the list and photo-cards variants already do) as a .process-step__marker before each .process-timeline__label, set in the accent colour; in patterns.css, give .process-timeline__row the room for it in its label column.

findings.issue: The fixed 14rem label column wraps several step labels onto a second line that holds one or two words ('Receive your free / quotation', 'Check service response / times', 'Review the details / together'), while the text column next to them has plenty of room.
findings.reference: The competitor's step titles sit on one line above their text.
findings.fix: In reference.css, size the label column to its words instead of 14rem: .block--process .process-timeline__row { grid-template-columns: minmax(14rem, max-content) 1fr; } with a max width (for example 22rem) so the text column keeps its line length.

findings.issue: This block has no heading, and its only intro line, 'From sign-off to bulk production' (a caption in the copy), is set as plain body text with a heading's spacing above the steps, so it looks like a stray sentence rather than the title of the sequence (the same at 390 px).
findings.reference: The competitor puts a clear label over each sequence: a heading, or uppercase UI labels on its timeline row.
findings.fix: In reference.css, style the lead of a process block that has no heading as a caption: .block--process:not(:has(h2)) > p (or the template's intro selector) { font-family: var(--font-ui); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 0.875rem; } so it reads as the sequence's label.
